question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'no substitution required'.

The unit twitched like a bird (preening it's plumage and becomes motionless).
option_1: preening its plumage and became motionless
option_3: preening it's plumage while becoming motionless
option_4: to preen it's plumage and becomes motionless
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. preening its plumage and became motionless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed part contains two errors, and only Option 1 corrects both.

◦ "it's" is the contraction of "it is / it has". The possessive adjective is "its" (without an apostrophe). The bird preens its (own) plumage. (अपने पंख)

◦ The main verb of the sentence is "twitched" — simple past. The verb joined to it by "and" must also be in the past tense, so "becomes" must become "became".

◦ Correct: The unit twitched like a bird preening its plumage and became motionless.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "No substitution required" is wrong because the printed segment has the "it's/its" error and a tense error.

• Option 3 keeps the wrong "it's" and changes the structure to "while becoming", which is still not parallel with "twitched".

• Option 4 keeps "it's" and also keeps the present-tense "becomes".

NOTE

• Remember the pair: its = belonging to it (The dog wagged its tail); it's = it is / it has (It's raining).

• Verbs joined by "and" in a sentence must normally stay in the same tense (parallelism): "He sat down and opened the book".

question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: Protest is also a saffety valve.
option_2: Protest is also a safety valvve.
option_3: Protast is also a safety valve.
option_4: Protest is also a safety valve.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Protest is also a safety valve.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Every word in Option 4 is spelt correctly — "protest" (an expression of objection/disagreement — विरोध), "safety" (the state of being safe — सुरक्षा) and "valve" (a device that controls the flow of a fluid — वाल्व).

◦ Correct: Protest is also a safety valve.

• Spelling keys: PRO + TEST, SAFE + TY (the final "e" of "safe" changes to "y-form" — safety, one "f"), VAL + VE.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 misspells "safety" as "saffety" (double "f" is wrong).

• Option 2 misspells "valve" as "valvve" (double "v" is wrong).

• Option 3 misspells "protest" as "protast" (the second vowel is "e", not "a").

NOTE

• "A safety valve" is also used figuratively for an outlet that releases pressure/tension harmlessly — hence "Protest is also a safety valve" in a democracy.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

That movie is so sad; the ending always makes me bawling.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. makes me bawl.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Make" is a causative verb. Its structure is make + object + bare infinitive (V1 without "to"). So it must be "makes me bawl", not "makes me bawling" / "makes me bawled".

◦ Correct: That movie is so sad; the ending always makes me bawl.

• "Bawl" means to weep or cry noisily. (ज़ोर-ज़ोर से रोना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "makes me bawled" wrongly uses the past participle after "make".

• Option 2 "No improvement" cannot be right because "makes me bawling" is ungrammatical.

• Option 4 "made me bawl" changes the tense; the adverb "always" with "is so sad" (present) requires the simple present "makes".

NOTE

• Verbs taking the bare infinitive: make, let, see, hear, watch, feel, help (help may take "to").

◦ e.g. "She made him apologise", "They let us go", "I saw her leave".

• In the passive, "make" takes the to-infinitive: "He was made to apologise".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym to substitute the bracketed word in the given sentence.

In the twentieth century, many (radical) intellectuals embraced the mass media.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. fanatical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Radical" here means holding extreme views; favouring drastic/complete change. Its closest synonym among the options is "fanatical" (extremely and uncritically zealous). (कट्टर / अतिवादी)

◦ Correct: In the twentieth century, many fanatical intellectuals embraced the mass media.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "sabbatical" = a period of paid leave granted for study or travel — unrelated.

• Option 2 "egotistical" = excessively self-centred/conceited — not the same as extreme in views.

• Option 3 "sceptical" = doubting, not easily convinced — it is almost the opposite of a zealous believer.

NOTE

• Synonyms of radical: fanatical, extremist, revolutionary, drastic, fundamental. Antonyms: moderate, conservative, superficial.

• Note the other sense of "radical" — basic/fundamental ("a radical change in policy").

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Police used ______ evidence to convict a victim who was innocent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. fabricated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fabricated" means invented or made up in order to deceive; falsified. Since the person convicted was innocent, the evidence used against him must have been false/made-up. (मनगढ़ंत / झूठा)

◦ Correct: Police used fabricated evidence to convict a victim who was innocent.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "stunted" = prevented from growing properly — does not collocate with "evidence".

• Option 3 "hateful" = arousing hatred — meaningless with "evidence" here.

• Option 4 "authentic" = genuine and true; genuine evidence would not convict an innocent person, so it contradicts the sentence.

NOTE

• Collocations with evidence: fabricated / circumstantial / conclusive / documentary / tampered evidence.

• Synonyms of fabricated: concocted, forged, trumped-up, falsified. Antonym: authentic, genuine.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Restoring soil health would help at mitigate the effects of climate change.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. help at mitigate the.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "help" is followed either by the bare infinitive or by the to-infinitive — never by a preposition. So "help at mitigate" is wrong; it must be "help mitigate" or "help to mitigate".

◦ Correct: Restoring soil health would help mitigate the effects of climate change.

• "Mitigate" means to make less severe; to lessen. (कम करना / शमन करना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Part 3 "Restoring soil health would" is correct — a gerund ("Restoring") is a fine subject and takes a singular verb.

• Part 2 "effects of climate change." is correct — "effects" (noun, results) is the right word here, not "affects".

• Since a clear error exists, Option 4 "No error" cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Verbs that take the bare infinitive after them include help, make, let, see, hear.

• Do not insert a preposition before an infinitive: "help to do / help do" — never "help at/for/in do".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Wheat is widely _______ but the output is not large.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. grown.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is in the passive voice ("is + past participle"), and crops are grown (cultivated). The contrast "but the output is not large" confirms that the topic is cultivation.

◦ Correct: Wheat is widely grown but the output is not large.

• "Grow – grew – grown"; here "grown" is the V3/past participle required after "is".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "gross" = total (before deductions) / very unpleasant — not a participle.

• Option 2 "grilled" = cooked on a grill; questioned intensively — wrong sense.

• Option 4 "groan" = a deep sound of pain (a verb/noun) and is not a past participle, so it cannot follow "is".

NOTE

• Watch the homophone pair grown (V3 of grow) and groan (to moan). Similarly gross vs grocer.

• Passive structure: is/am/are/was/were + V3 — "Rice is grown in Bengal".

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

The young of a frog
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Tadpole.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "tadpole" is the young (larval stage) of a frog or toad — it lives in water, has a tail and gills, and later develops into a frog through metamorphosis. (मेंढक का बच्चा / टैडपोल)

◦ Example: The pond was full of tadpoles in the rainy season.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Kitten" is the young of a cat.

• Option 2 "Pup/puppy" is the young of a dog (also of seals and some other animals).

• Option 4 "Antelope" is a separate animal altogether, not the young of anything.

NOTE

• Common young ones: calf (cow/elephant), cub (lion/tiger/bear), foal (horse), lamb (sheep), kid (goat), chick (hen), duckling (duck), cygnet (swan), joey (kangaroo).

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose 'No improvement' as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

It is the most effective means of mass communication.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined part "the most effective" is already correct. A superlative adjective takes "the" before it, and the adjective "effective" correctly qualifies the noun "means".

◦ Correct (as printed): It is the most effective means of mass communication.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a most effecting" — "effecting" is a verb form (to effect = to bring about) and "a" is wrong before a superlative used with a defined noun.

• Option 2 "a most effectives" — adjectives are never pluralised in English ("effectives" is wrong).

• Option 3 "the most effectively" — an adverb cannot qualify the noun "means"; an adjective is required.

NOTE

• Degrees: effective – more effective – the most effective.

• Note "means" (a method/way) is the same in singular and plural: "a means of transport", "many means of transport".

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

Adding aloe vera gel will prevent the hand sanitizer of drying out your skin.
option_3: will prevent the hand sanitizer of
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. will prevent the hand sanitizer of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "prevent" takes the preposition "from", not "of": prevent + object + from + V-ing.

◦ Correct: Adding aloe vera gel will prevent the hand sanitizer from drying out your skin.

• "Prevent" means to stop something from happening. (रोकना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Part 4 "Adding aloe vera gel" is correct — a gerund phrase working as the subject.

• Part 2 "drying out your skin." is correct — after "from", the -ing form is required.

• Since a clear preposition error exists, Option 1 "No error" is not possible.

NOTE

• Verb + from + V-ing: prevent, stop, keep, discourage, prohibit, refrain (from).

• Compare: "deprive somebody of something", "accuse somebody of something" — those take "of", but "prevent" does not.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Viscous
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Watery.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Viscous" means thick, sticky and semi-fluid in consistency; not flowing freely (like honey or syrup). Its antonym is "watery" — thin and flowing freely like water. (गाढ़ा का विलोम — पतला/पनीला)

◦ Example: Honey is viscous, whereas buttermilk is watery.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "Thick" is a synonym of viscous, not its antonym — a common trap.

• Option 1 "Grim" (stern, gloomy) and Option 2 "Brutal" (savagely violent) are unrelated to consistency.

NOTE

• Synonyms of viscous: thick, sticky, gluey, glutinous, syrupy. Antonyms: watery, thin, runny, fluid.

• In science, "viscosity" is a liquid's resistance to flow; oil has high viscosity, water low.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

Make sure that you always challenge yourself.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Question.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As a verb, "challenge" means to question or dispute something; to call it into question / to test it. So "challenge yourself" carries the sense of "question (and test) yourself". (चुनौती देना / प्रश्न करना)

◦ Example: A good student will challenge/question received ideas instead of accepting them blindly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Carry" (to transport/bear) does not match the sense of challenge.

• Option 2 "Approve" (to agree to / accept) is the opposite idea — approving means not questioning.

• Option 4 "Place" (to put) is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of challenge (verb): question, dispute, dare, defy, contest, test. As a noun it means a difficult task or an invitation to compete.

• Antonyms: accept, approve, agree, endorse.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Tending to associate with others of one's kind
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Gregarious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gregarious" means fond of company; sociable; (of animals) living in flocks or herds — i.e., tending to associate with others of one's own kind. (मिलनसार / यूथचारी)

◦ Example: Sheep are gregarious animals; my gregarious cousin makes friends everywhere.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Pedantic" = excessively concerned with minor rules and details.

• Option 2 "Pungent" = having a sharp, strong smell or taste.

• Option 4 "Venial" = (of a fault or sin) slight and pardonable.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: misanthrope (one who hates mankind), recluse/hermit (one who lives alone), extrovert (an outgoing person), introvert (a reserved person).

• Antonyms of gregarious: solitary, unsociable, reclusive.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

In my opinion, you should went for higher studies in London.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. you should went for.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A modal auxiliary ("should") is always followed by the base form (V1) of the verb. "went" is the past tense (V2), so it must be replaced by "go".

◦ Correct: In my opinion, you should go for higher studies in London.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Part 2 "In my opinion," is a correct introductory phrase.

• Part 4 "higher studies in London." is correct — "higher studies" is standard and "in London" is the right preposition for a city.

• Since a clear error exists, Option 1 "No error" is not possible.

NOTE

• Modals: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would, must, ought to — all take V1 after them ("must go", "can swim", "should write").

• For the past sense use modal + have + V3: "You should have gone last year".

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

The person driving the car ______ control over the wheels and knocked her down.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. lost.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is the main verb of the sentence, and it is joined by "and" to "knocked" (simple past). For parallelism the blank must also be in the simple past — "lost".

◦ Correct: The person driving the car lost control over the wheels and knocked her down.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "lose" (present, V1) does not agree with the past-tense "knocked".

• Option 3 "losing" is a participle and cannot stand as the main verb without an auxiliary.

• Option 4 "loose" is an adjective meaning "not tight" — an entirely different word from the verb "lose".

NOTE

• Remember: lose (verb — to be deprived of; lose–lost–lost) vs loose (adjective — not tight). "Do not lose your keys"; "The shirt is loose".

• "Lose control over/of" is the standard collocation.

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

A blind spot
option_2: A person with no emotional feelings
option_3: A situation where no progress is made
option_4: An area in your range of vision that you cannot see properly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. An area in your range of vision that you cannot see properly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "A blind spot" literally means an area that you cannot see properly, especially the part of the road that a driver cannot see in the mirrors. Figuratively it means a subject about which a person is ignorant or prejudiced. (दृष्टि-दोष क्षेत्र / अंध क्षेत्र)

◦ Example: Always check your blind spot before changing lanes.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is a literal misreading — a blind spot is a place/area, not a person.

• Option 2 "a person with no emotional feelings" would be "cold-hearted / stone-hearted".

• Option 3 "a situation where no progress is made" is the idiom "deadlock / stalemate".

NOTE

• In biology, the "blind spot" is the point where the optic nerve leaves the retina — it has no light-sensitive cells, so no image forms there.

• Related idioms: "turn a blind eye" (to ignore deliberately), "blind alley" (a course leading nowhere).

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate choice.

His intent was to become sole lord and to ______ his tiny principality.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. aggrandize.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Aggrandize" means to increase the power, wealth, status or size of something/somebody. A ruler who wants to be "sole lord" would naturally wish to enlarge his tiny principality. (शक्ति/विस्तार बढ़ाना)

◦ Correct: His intent was to become sole lord and to aggrandize his tiny principality.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "subsidize" = to support financially with a subsidy — does not fit an ambition for power.

• Option 3 "jeopardize" = to put at risk — the opposite of what an ambitious ruler wants for his own state.

• Option 4 "methodize" = to arrange in an orderly manner — too weak and out of context.

NOTE

• Synonyms of aggrandize: enlarge, expand, magnify, exalt, augment. Antonyms: diminish, reduce, belittle.

• "Self-aggrandizement" = the act of increasing one's own power or importance.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The arms and legs lay in a careless way.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Vigilant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Careless" means not giving sufficient attention or thought; negligent. Its antonym is "vigilant" — watchful, alert and careful about possible danger. (लापरवाह का विलोम — सतर्क)

◦ Example: A careless driver causes accidents; a vigilant driver avoids them.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 3 "Forgetful" and Option 4 "Neglectful" are synonyms of careless, not antonyms — classic distractors.

• Option 2 "Unsafe" describes a condition of danger, not a person's attentiveness.

NOTE

• Synonyms of careless: negligent, thoughtless, heedless, slapdash, reckless. Antonyms: careful, cautious, vigilant, attentive, meticulous.

• "Vigilance" gives us "Vigilance Commission" — a watchdog body against corruption.

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Tihgt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Tihgt" is misspelt; the correct spelling is "Tight", meaning firmly fixed, closely fitting or stretched. (कसा हुआ / तंग)

◦ Correct: Please keep the lid tight.

• Spelling key: T + I + GH + T — the "gh" comes before the final "t" (as in light, night, sight, fight, right).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Locker" (a small lockable cupboard), "Rift" (a crack, split or serious disagreement) and "Stock" (a supply of goods; shares) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• The "-ight" family: bright, fright, might, slight, height (h-e-i-g-h-t). Note that "height" ends in "-ght" but is spelt with "ei".

• "Rift" is common in the news: "Rift Valley" (a large geological trough, e.g., the Great Rift Valley of Africa).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Get down to brass tacks
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To become serious about something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "get down to brass tacks" means to start discussing the most important, practical details of a matter; to become serious about the real business. (असली मुद्दे पर आना)

◦ Example: After the introductions, the committee got down to brass tacks and fixed the budget.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Get fired from the job" corresponds to idioms like "get the sack / be given the boot".

• Option 3 "Compromise, cooperation between people" corresponds to "meet halfway / give and take".

• Option 4 "To be ready" corresponds to "gear up / all set".

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "get down to business", "cut to the chase", "come to the point".

• The phrase is believed to come from the brass tacks used in upholstery or in shops to measure cloth — i.e., getting to the basic facts.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Salvador Dali (1)________ a prominent Spanish surrealist painter (2)________ in Figueres, Catalonia, on 11 May 1904. Dali's father was strict in the education of his children unlike (3)________ mother. Dali had a brother named Salvador (4)________ was born nine months before him and died of gastroenteritis. When he was five, Dalí was taken to his brother's grave and was told that he was his brother's (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage narrates events of 1904 — a completed past time — so the simple past is required. The subject "Salvador Dali" is singular, so the correct past form of "be" is "was".

◦ Correct: Salvador Dali was a prominent Spanish surrealist painter born in Figueres ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "were" is the plural past form and does not agree with the singular subject.

• Option 4 "is" is present tense — wrong for a painter born in 1904 and long dead.

• Option 3 "has" cannot be followed directly by the noun phrase "a prominent Spanish surrealist painter" in this structure.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement for "be": I/he/she/it + was; we/you/they + were (past); he/she/it + is; they + are (present).

• Salvador Dalí (1904–1989) was the famous Spanish Surrealist painter of "The Persistence of Memory" (the melting clocks).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Salvador Dali (1)________ a prominent Spanish surrealist painter (2)________ in Figueres, Catalonia, on 11 May 1904. Dali's father was strict in the education of his children unlike (3)________ mother. Dali had a brother named Salvador (4)________ was born nine months before him and died of gastroenteritis. When he was five, Dalí was taken to his brother's grave and was told that he was his brother's (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. born.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is followed by a place ("in Figueres, Catalonia") and a date of birth ("on 11 May 1904"), so the required word is "born" — the past participle used for coming into the world.

◦ Correct: ... a prominent Spanish surrealist painter born in Figueres, Catalonia, on 11 May 1904.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "rooted" (firmly fixed) does not go with a date of birth.

• Option 2 "bought" (past of buy) and Option 3 "brought" (past of bring) make no sense with a birthplace and are common spelling/meaning confusions.

NOTE

• "Born" is used in the passive: "He was born in 1904"; as a reduced relative it becomes "a painter (who was) born in Figueres".

• Distinguish born (given birth to) from borne (carried/endured — "water-borne diseases").

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Salvador Dali (1)________ a prominent Spanish surrealist painter (2)________ in Figueres, Catalonia, on 11 May 1904. Dali's father was strict in the education of his children unlike (3)________ mother. Dali had a brother named Salvador (4)________ was born nine months before him and died of gastroenteritis. When he was five, Dalí was taken to his brother's grave and was told that he was his brother's (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. his.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank comes before the noun "mother", so a possessive adjective is needed, and it must refer back to Dali (a male, singular) — hence "his mother".

◦ Correct: Dali's father was strict in the education of his children unlike his mother.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "him" and Option 3 "her" — "him" is an object pronoun (never used before a noun) and "her", though possessive, would wrongly refer to a female.

• Option 1 "their" is plural and has no plural antecedent here; the contrast is between Dali's father and Dali's mother.

NOTE

• Possessive adjectives: my, our, your, his, her, its, their — always placed before a noun.

• Object pronouns: me, us, you, him, her, it, them — used after a verb or preposition.

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Salvador Dali (1)________ a prominent Spanish surrealist painter (2)________ in Figueres, Catalonia, on 11 May 1904. Dali's father was strict in the education of his children unlike (3)________ mother. Dali had a brother named Salvador (4)________ was born nine months before him and died of gastroenteritis. When he was five, Dalí was taken to his brother's grave and was told that he was his brother's (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. who.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank introduces a relative clause whose subject is missing ("____ was born nine months before him"). For a person acting as the subject, the correct relative pronoun is "who".

◦ Correct: Dali had a brother named Salvador who was born nine months before him ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "whose" shows possession and would need a noun after it ("whose birth ...").

• Option 3 "whom" is the object form ("the brother whom he never met").

• Option 4 "that" is grammatically possible in some clauses but is not preferred after a named person in a non-defining, descriptive clause; "who" is the appropriate choice here.

NOTE

• Relative pronouns: who (subject – person), whom (object – person), whose (possessive), which (things), that (people/things in defining clauses).

question:
In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

Salvador Dali (1)________ a prominent Spanish surrealist painter (2)________ in Figueres, Catalonia, on 11 May 1904. Dali's father was strict in the education of his children unlike (3)________ mother. Dali had a brother named Salvador (4)________ was born nine months before him and died of gastroenteritis. When he was five, Dalí was taken to his brother's grave and was told that he was his brother's (5)________.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. reincarnation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reincarnation" means rebirth of a soul in a new body. The famous anecdote is that the five-year-old Dalí was taken to his dead brother's grave and told that he was his brother's reincarnation — i.e., his brother born again. (पुनर्जन्म)

◦ Correct: ... he was told that he was his brother's reincarnation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "ordination" = the ceremony of making someone a priest.

• Option 2 "detonation" = an explosion.

• Option 4 "stagnation" = the state of not flowing or not developing.

NOTE

• Word family: incarnate/incarnation (embodiment in flesh), re- (again) + incarnation = born again in another body.

• This childhood incident is often cited as an influence on Dalí's Surrealist imagery.

question: Twenty five percent of the land revenue collected by Marathas in the Deccan was called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chauth.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chauth" was a tax equal to one-fourth (25%) of the land revenue, levied by the Marathas on territories in the Deccan (and beyond) in return for a promise not to raid them. (चौथ — भू-राजस्व का 25%)

• The word itself comes from "chautha", meaning "a fourth".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Sardeshmukhi" was an additional levy of 10% of the land revenue, claimed by Shivaji as the hereditary "Sardeshmukh" (chief headman) of Maharashtra.

• Together, Chauth (25%) + Sardeshmukhi (10%) = 35% of the revenue of the areas concerned.

• "Bhoga" in ancient India referred to the king's share of produce/periodical supplies; "Bhaga" was the king's share of the produce (usually one-sixth).

NOTE

• Shivaji (1630–1680) founded the Maratha kingdom and was crowned Chhatrapati at Raigad in 1674; his revenue and military systems (Ashta Pradhan council, Chauth, Sardeshmukhi) are frequently asked in SSC exams.

question: 'The Race of My Life' is an autobiography of famous Indian athlete ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Milkha Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Race of My Life" is the autobiography of the legendary Indian sprinter Milkha Singh, popularly called "The Flying Sikh". It was co-written with his daughter Sonia Sanwalka. (मिल्खा सिंह की आत्मकथा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Milkha Singh won gold at the 1958 Asian Games and the 1958 Commonwealth Games and famously finished fourth in the 400 m final at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

• He was awarded the Padma Shri (1959). The film "Bhaag Milkha Bhaag" (2013) is based on his life.

NOTE

• Other sports autobiographies: "Ace Against Odds" (Sania Mirza), "The Test of My Life" (Yuvraj Singh), "Straight from the Heart" (Kapil Dev), "Playing It My Way" (Sachin Tendulkar), "Unbreakable" (Mary Kom).

question:
Fungi can grow on which of the following items?

I. Bread

II. Pickles

III. Leather

IV. Clothes

Select the correct option.
solution_text:
The correct answer is I, II, III and IV.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fungi are saprophytic/heterotrophic organisms that grow on almost any organic surface when there is moisture, warmth and organic matter. They can therefore grow on bread, pickles, leather and clothes — all four items. (कवक — फफूंदी)

◦ Bread mould (Rhizopus), the white/greenish growth on damp leather and clothes (mildew), and the fungal film on pickles are common examples.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Fungi lack chlorophyll, so they cannot make their own food; they absorb nutrients from dead organic matter (saprophytes) or from living hosts (parasites).

• Examples: Mushroom, Yeast (Saccharomyces), Penicillium, Aspergillus, Rhizopus.

NOTE

• Yeast is used in baking and brewing; Penicillium notatum gave the world the antibiotic penicillin (discovered by Alexander Fleming, 1928).

• Keeping food dry and airtight prevents fungal growth — hence pickles are stored in oil and kept moisture-free.

question: In August 2022, Prime Minister of India inaugurated Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospital in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In August 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospital and Research Centre at New Chandigarh, Mohali (Punjab). It is run by the Tata Memorial Centre under the Department of Atomic Energy. (मोहाली, पंजाब)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The hospital was built to give affordable cancer care to patients of Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir, reducing the load on PGIMER Chandigarh.

• It is named after Dr. Homi Jehangir Bhabha, the "Father of the Indian Nuclear Programme" and founder of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) and the Atomic Energy Establishment, Trombay (now BARC).

NOTE

• The Tata Memorial Hospital, Mumbai, is India's premier cancer treatment and research centre; Homi Bhabha Cancer Hospitals function as its regional units.

question: Which among the following is an agricultural festival of Arunachal Pradesh and celebrated by the Galo tribe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mopin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mopin" is the popular agricultural festival of the Galo tribe of Arunachal Pradesh, celebrated in April to drive away evil spirits and pray for a rich harvest, prosperity and the well-being of the community. (मोपिन — अरुणाचल प्रदेश)

• People smear each other with rice powder and perform the Popir dance; the rice beer "Apong" is served.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Losar" is the New Year festival of the Monpa tribe (and of Tibetan Buddhists) in Arunachal Pradesh.

• Option 2 "Ugadi" is the New Year of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka.

• Option 3 "Karma" is a tribal festival of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Madhya Pradesh, worshipping the Karam tree.

NOTE

• Other festivals of Arunachal Pradesh: Solung (Adi tribe), Nyokum (Nyishi tribe), Dree (Apatani tribe), Boori Boot (Hill Miri), Reh (Idu Mishmi).

question: The Xinjiang region, which was seen in the news due to the collapse of a gold mine, is located in which country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Xinjiang" (officially the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region) is the largest administrative region of China, located in the north-west of the country. (शिनजियांग — चीन)

• It is rich in minerals, coal, oil and gold, and mine accidents there are often reported in the news.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Xinjiang shares borders with Mongolia, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Afghanistan, Pakistan and India (Ladakh).

• It is home to the Uyghur Muslim community; its capital is Urumqi, and the Taklamakan Desert and the ancient Silk Route pass through it.

NOTE

• Other Chinese regions frequently in the news: Tibet (Xizang), Inner Mongolia, Hong Kong, Macau and the disputed Aksai Chin (claimed by India, administered by China).

question: Gair dance is performed by the ______ community of Rajasthan.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhil.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gair" is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed chiefly by the Bhil community, especially during Holi and Janmashtami. Dancers move in a circle with sticks, striking them in rhythm to the beat of drums. (गैर नृत्य — भील समुदाय)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Bhils are one of India's largest tribal groups, found in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Maharashtra. They were skilled archers and were known as allies of Maharana Pratap.

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan: Ghoomar (Bhil/Rajput women), Kalbeliya (Kalbeliya/snake-charmer community — UNESCO Intangible Heritage), Kathputli, Chari, Terah Taali, Bhavai.

NOTE

• Option 2 "Gond" is a tribe mainly of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh; the Jat and Gujjar are agricultural/pastoral communities of north India — none of them is associated with the Gair dance.

question: Offences for which the police can arrest a person without an order of the court are called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cognizable offences.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In a "cognizable offence", the police can register an FIR, investigate and arrest the accused without a warrant or an order of the court. These are usually serious offences. (संज्ञेय अपराध)

◦ Examples: murder, rape, dowry death, kidnapping, theft, rioting, waging war against the State.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• In a "non-cognizable offence" the police cannot arrest without a warrant and cannot start an investigation without the permission of a magistrate. Examples: defamation, public nuisance, simple hurt, cheating (in some forms).

• The classification is given in the First Schedule of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973, now replaced by the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

NOTE

• Other useful pairs: bailable vs non-bailable offences and compoundable vs non-compoundable offences.

• An FIR (First Information Report) under Section 154 CrPC can be registered only for a cognizable offence.

question: 'Eskimos' are associated with which geographical region?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Polar Region.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Eskimos" (now generally called the Inuit) are the indigenous people of the Polar/Arctic region — northern Canada, Greenland, Alaska (USA) and Siberia (Russia). (ध्रुवीय प्रदेश)

• They live in snow houses called "igloos", wear fur clothing (parka), travel on sledges pulled by huskies and depend on hunting and fishing (seal, walrus, caribou, fish).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Bushmen live in the Kalahari Desert, Bedouins in the Arabian/Sahara deserts (arid region), Masai in the East African savanna, and Pygmies/Semang/Boro in tropical rainforests (Congo Basin, Amazon Basin, Malaysia).

NOTE

• Polar regions have tundra vegetation — mosses, lichens and small shrubs — and experience the midnight sun in summer and long nights in winter.

question: According to the Ashokan Inscription which of the following was NOT a provincial centre in Magadha Empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indraprastha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to Ashokan inscriptions, the Mauryan (Magadhan) empire had its capital at Pataliputra and four/five provincial centres: Taxila (north-west), Ujjayini (west), Tosali (east, in Kalinga), Suvarnagiri (south) and Samapa. "Indraprastha" was not among them. (इंद्रप्रस्थ — मौर्य प्रांतीय केंद्र नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Indraprastha is associated with the Mahabharata — the capital of the Pandavas, traditionally identified with the area around present-day Delhi (Purana Qila).

• Provinces were governed by princes of royal blood called "Kumara/Aryaputra", assisted by Mahamatras and Rajukas.

NOTE

• Ashoka (r. c. 268–232 BCE) issued the Major and Minor Rock Edicts and Pillar Edicts in Prakrit language, mostly in the Brahmi script (also Kharosthi, Greek and Aramaic in the north-west). They were deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

question: Ilyas Khan was born in Lucknow to a family of musicians. He was famous for playing ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ustad Ilyas Khan, born in Lucknow into a well-known family of musicians, was a celebrated sitar player of Hindustani classical music. (सितार वादक)

• The sitar is a long-necked plucked string instrument with sympathetic strings and movable frets, and is the best-known melodic instrument of North Indian classical music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other famous sitar maestros: Pandit Ravi Shankar, Ustad Vilayat Khan, Ustad Shahid Parvez, Nikhil Banerjee, Anoushka Shankar.

• Instrument categories: Tabla and Mridangam are percussion (Avanaddha) instruments; Veena and Sitar are string (Tata) instruments; the flute is a wind (Sushir) instrument.

NOTE

• Famous exponents: Tabla — Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha, Kishan Maharaj; Veena — S. Balachander, Chitti Babu; Mridangam — Palghat Mani Iyer, Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman.

question: 'Magnus Carlsen' is associated with which of the following games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chess.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Magnus Carlsen of Norway is a chess grandmaster who became World Chess Champion in 2013 (defeating Viswanathan Anand) and retained the title until he chose not to defend it in 2023. (शतरंज)

• He became a Grandmaster at the age of 13 and has held the highest FIDE rating in history (2882).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Chess is governed by FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs), founded in 1924; International Chess Day is 20 July.

• Viswanathan Anand was India's first Grandmaster (1988) and a five-time World Champion; R. Praggnanandhaa, D. Gukesh and Arjun Erigaisi are leading young Indian players. D. Gukesh became World Champion in 2024.

NOTE

• The game of chess is believed to have originated in India as "Chaturanga" during the Gupta period.

question: According to the World Bank classification 2020-2021, India belongs to the category of _______ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is lower-middle income country.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the World Bank classification for 2020-2021, India is a "lower-middle income country". The World Bank classifies economies on the basis of Gross National Income (GNI) per capita, calculated by the Atlas method. (निम्न-मध्यम आय वर्ग)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The four World Bank income groups are: low income, lower-middle income, upper-middle income and high income.

• The World Bank was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference; its headquarters is in Washington D.C. It publishes the World Development Report and the Ease of Doing Business rankings (discontinued in 2021).

NOTE

• The World Bank Group has five institutions: IBRD, IDA, IFC, MIGA and ICSID. The IMF is its Bretton Woods twin, dealing with balance-of-payments support.

question: Which country hosted the 1982 edition of the Asian Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 9th Asian Games (1982) were hosted by India at New Delhi — the second time India hosted the Games. The mascot was "Appu" (an elephant), and this edition is remembered for the introduction of colour television in India. (1982 एशियाई खेल — नई दिल्ली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• India also hosted the first Asian Games in 1951 at New Delhi, where the mascot-era had not yet begun; the Games were then conceived by Prof. G. D. Sondhi.

• The Asian Games are held every four years and are organised by the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).

NOTE

• Recent editions: 2014 Incheon (South Korea), 2018 Jakarta–Palembang (Indonesia), 2022 Hangzhou (China, held in 2023); the 2026 Games are to be held in Aichi–Nagoya, Japan.

question: In the 18th century, the development of cotton industries in Britain resulted in ______.
option_1: Increase in demand of Indian textile in Britain
option_2: Decline of textiles production in India
option_3: Increase in demand of Indian textile in India
option_4: Decline of British textiles industries in India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Decline of textiles production in India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Industrial Revolution in Britain mechanised cotton spinning and weaving in the 18th century, producing cheap machine-made cloth. Heavy import duties in Britain on Indian cloth and the flooding of Indian markets with British goods ruined Indian weavers and caused the decline of textile production in India — a process called de-industrialisation. (भारतीय वस्त्र उद्योग का पतन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Key inventions: Spinning Jenny (James Hargreaves), Water Frame (Richard Arkwright), Spinning Mule (Samuel Crompton), Power Loom (Edmund Cartwright) and the Steam Engine (James Watt).

• Indian centres such as Dhaka (muslin), Murshidabad, Surat and Machilipatnam decayed; weavers were forced into agriculture, increasing pressure on land.

NOTE

• India was turned into a supplier of raw materials (raw cotton, indigo, jute) and a market for finished British goods — the classic colonial "drain of wealth" pattern described by Dadabhai Naoroji.

question: The normal temperature of the human body is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 37° C.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The normal temperature of the human body is about 37° C, which equals 98.6° F. (मानव शरीर का सामान्य तापमान — 37° सेल्सियस)

• Conversion: F = (9/5) × C + 32 → (9/5) × 37 + 32 = 66.6 + 32 = 98.6° F.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Body temperature is regulated by the "hypothalamus" in the brain, which acts as the body's thermostat.

• A clinical thermometer normally has a range of about 35° C to 42° C (94° F to 108° F) and contains a kink to stop the mercury from falling back.

NOTE

• Other reference points: water freezes at 0° C (32° F) and boils at 100° C (212° F) at sea level; -40° C = -40° F (the only equal point). Absolute zero is 0 K = -273.15° C.

question: How many biosphere reserves are there in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eighteen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India has 18 biosphere reserves, notified by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to conserve biodiversity along with the traditional life of local communities. (18 जैवमंडल आरक्षित क्षेत्र)

• The first biosphere reserve of India was the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (1986).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A biosphere reserve has three zones: core zone (strictly protected), buffer zone (limited research/education activity) and transition zone (human settlement and sustainable use).

• Twelve Indian biosphere reserves are on the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere (MAB) World Network, including Nilgiri, Gulf of Mannar, Sundarbans, Nanda Devi, Nokrek, Pachmarhi, Similipal, Achanakmar-Amarkantak, Great Nicobar, Agasthyamalai, Khangchendzonga and Panna.

NOTE

• India also has 106 National Parks, 500+ Wildlife Sanctuaries, 55+ Tiger Reserves (Project Tiger, 1973) and 33 Elephant Reserves (Project Elephant, 1992).

question: The Temple at Khajuraho were built during which dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandella dynasty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous temples of Khajuraho (Chhatarpur district, Madhya Pradesh) were built between about 950 and 1050 CE by the rulers of the Chandella dynasty of Bundelkhand. (चंदेल राजवंश — खजुराहो)

• They are built in the Nagara style of temple architecture and are renowned for their exquisite sculptures.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Khajuraho Group of Monuments was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1986.

• The largest and most famous temple is the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple; other important ones are the Lakshmana, Vishvanatha, Chausath Yogini and the Jain Parshvanatha temples.

• Prominent Chandella rulers: Yashovarman, Dhanga, Vidyadhara and Paramardi (Parmal), whose court is linked with the warriors Alha and Udal.

NOTE

• Temple styles: Nagara (North India, curvilinear shikhara), Dravida (South India, pyramidal vimana with gopurams) and Vesara (a hybrid style of the Deccan).

question: As per Budget 2023-24, how much comes from corporation tax for every 1 Re receipt of the government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15 paisa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the Union Budget 2023-24, the "Rupee Comes From" chart showed that corporation tax contributes 15 paise of every 1 rupee of government receipts. (निगम कर — 15 पैसे)

• Corporation tax is the direct tax levied on the profits of companies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• As per the same Budget 2023-24 chart, the biggest sources were borrowings and other liabilities (34 paise), GST (17 paise), income tax (15 paise), corporation tax (15 paise), union excise duties (7 paise), customs (4 paise) and non-tax receipts (6 paise).

• The Budget 2023-24 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2023.

NOTE

• Direct taxes (income tax, corporation tax) are paid directly by the assessee and are governed by the CBDT; indirect taxes (GST, customs) are collected through intermediaries and are governed by the CBIC.

• The Budget is presented under Article 112 of the Constitution as the "Annual Financial Statement".

question: In which type of farming, the land is used for growing food and fodder crops and rearing livestock?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mixed farming.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In "mixed farming", the same farm is used both for growing crops (food and fodder) and for rearing livestock. The two activities support each other — fodder feeds the animals, and animal manure fertilises the fields. (मिश्रित कृषि)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Dairy farming" concentrates only on milch animals and milk production.

• "Plantation farming" grows a single cash crop on a large estate (tea, coffee, rubber, sugarcane, spices) using much capital and labour.

• "Commercial farming" is farming mainly for sale in the market rather than for the farmer's own use.

NOTE

• Other types of farming: subsistence farming (for the farmer's own needs), shifting cultivation (jhum/slash-and-burn), intensive and extensive farming, horticulture (fruits/vegetables) and sericulture (silkworm rearing).

question: Which of the following is 'NOT' one of the three major types of rocks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Magnetic Rocks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The three major types of rocks are Igneous, Sedimentary and Metamorphic. "Magnetic rocks" is not one of them. (आग्नेय, अवसादी और कायांतरित — तीन प्रमुख प्रकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Igneous rocks" form from the cooling and solidification of magma/lava — they are called primary rocks (e.g., granite, basalt, gabbro).

• "Sedimentary rocks" form from the compaction and cementation of sediments and often contain fossils (e.g., sandstone, limestone, shale).

• "Metamorphic rocks" form when existing rocks change under great heat and pressure (e.g., limestone → marble, coal → diamond/graphite, shale → slate, granite → gneiss, sandstone → quartzite).

NOTE

• The continuous transformation of one rock type into another is called the "rock cycle". Magnetite (an iron ore) is only a magnetic mineral, not a rock class.

question: Karagam Folk Dance is associated with which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tamil Nadu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Karagam (Karagattam)" is a folk dance of Tamil Nadu in which dancers balance a decorated pot (karagam) on their heads while dancing, traditionally in honour of Mariamman, the goddess of rain and health. (करगम — तमिलनाडु)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Tamil Nadu: Kummi, Kolattam, Oyilattam, Mayilattam (peacock dance), Devarattam, Poikal Kudirai Attam and the classical Bharatanatyam.

• Folk dances of the other options: Rajasthan — Ghoomar, Kalbeliya, Gair; Assam — Bihu, Bagurumba; Haryana — Khoria, Dhamal, Phag.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms are Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: The cells having well - organized nucleus with a nuclear membrane are designated as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is eukaryotic cells.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cells that have a well-organised (true) nucleus enclosed by a nuclear membrane, along with membrane-bound organelles, are called "eukaryotic cells". (सुकेंद्रकी कोशिकाएँ)

• The word comes from Greek eu (true) + karyon (nucleus).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Prokaryotic cells" have no nuclear membrane and no membrane-bound organelles; their genetic material lies free in the cytoplasm as a nucleoid (e.g., bacteria and blue-green algae/cyanobacteria).

• Eukaryotes include all plants, animals, fungi and protists. "Cheek cells" are an example of human eukaryotic cells, not the scientific category asked for, and "autokaryotic cells" is not a valid term.

NOTE

• The cell was discovered by Robert Hooke (1665); Anton van Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells; Robert Brown (1831) discovered the nucleus; the cell theory was given by Schleiden and Schwann (1838-39) and extended by Virchow (1855).

question: In the Preamble of the Indian Constitution, ______ assures the dignity of the individual.
solution_text:
The correct answer is fraternity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Preamble of the Indian Constitution resolves to promote among all citizens "FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and integrity of the Nation". So it is fraternity that assures the dignity of the individual. (बंधुत्व — व्यक्ति की गरिमा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Preamble describes India as a SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC and secures for its citizens JUSTICE (social, economic and political), LIBERTY (of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship), EQUALITY (of status and of opportunity) and FRATERNITY.

• The words "Socialist, Secular and Integrity" were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

NOTE

• The ideals of Liberty, Equality and Fraternity were drawn from the French Revolution; the Preamble is based on the Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru (13 December 1946).

• In the Berubari Union case (1960) the Supreme Court held the Preamble was not a part of the Constitution, but in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) it held that it is a part of it.

question: First session of Indian National congress held in______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bombay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first session of the Indian National Congress (INC) was held in December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay (Mumbai), with 72 delegates attending. (भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस का पहला अधिवेशन — बंबई, 1885)

• Its first president was W. C. Bonnerjee, and the organisation was founded by A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The second session (1886) was held at Calcutta under Dadabhai Naoroji, and the third (1887) at Madras under Badruddin Tyabji, the first Muslim president of the INC.

• The Surat session (1907) saw the famous split between the Moderates and the Extremists; the Lahore session (1929), presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted the resolution of "Purna Swaraj".

NOTE

• Other landmark sessions: Calcutta (1906) — Swaraj declared as the goal under Dadabhai Naoroji; Lucknow (1916) — Congress-League Pact; Nagpur (1920) — Non-Cooperation; Karachi (1931) — Fundamental Rights resolution.
